about: Soho and Mayfair: a morning meeting off Oxford Circus, lunch in Soho, coffee on Carnaby Street.

cards.line: Did you know, the Beatles played their last ever public gig as a band on a Savile Row rooftop?
cards.fact: On 30 January 1969 the Beatles played on the roof of their Apple offices at 3 Savile Row. After 42 minutes, police told them to turn it down. It was the band's last public performance.

cards.line: Did you know, the statue of Charles II in Soho Square once stood in a fountain?
cards.fact: The statue of Charles II was once the centrepiece of a fountain in the middle of Soho Square, built in 1681. The fountain was a modest copy of a famous one in Rome.
cards.source: Wikipedia: Statue of Charles II, Soho Square

cards.line: Did you know, a Time magazine cover story made Carnaby Street world famous in 1966?
cards.fact: On 15 April 1966 a Time magazine cover story made Carnaby Street internationally famous, as the heart of Swinging London, where bands like the Who and the Rolling Stones shopped.

cards.line: Did you know, Jimi Hendrix's last ever public performance was at Ronnie Scott's in Soho?
cards.fact: Ronnie Scott's jazz club has been in Soho since 1959, and on Frith Street since 1965. Jimi Hendrix's last public performance was there, in 1970.

cards.line: Did you know, the Beatles recorded Hey Jude in a Soho side street, not at Abbey Road?
cards.fact: In 1968 the Beatles recorded Hey Jude at Trident Studios in St Anne's Court, Soho, because it had an eight-track machine. Abbey Road still only had four tracks.

about: Over Waterloo Bridge into the City, then east along Whitechapel Road to Bow.

cards.line: Did you know, a writer was assassinated with an umbrella on Waterloo Bridge?
cards.fact: In 1978 the Bulgarian writer Georgi Markov was waiting for a bus on Waterloo Bridge when a man used an umbrella to put a tiny pellet of poison into his leg.
cards.source: Wikipedia: Georgi Markov; Wikipedia: Waterloo Bridge

cards.line: Did you know, a Roman temple on Walbrook was moved away, then brought back?
cards.fact: A Roman temple to the god Mithras was found on Walbrook in 1954 and moved 100 metres for an office block. In 2017 it went back to its original site, underground.

cards.line: Did you know, a man was called back from a secret RAF mission to run a Shoreditch coffee stall?
cards.fact: Syd's coffee stall stood on Calvert Avenue, Shoreditch, for 100 years. In the war, the mayor got Syd's son called back from a secret RAF mission to run it.

cards.line: Did you know, a pub in Bromley-by-Bow hangs up a hot cross bun every Good Friday?
cards.fact: The Widow's Son is named after a widow who kept a hot cross bun for her sailor son, due home at Easter. Every Good Friday, the pub hangs up another.

cards.line: Did you know, Ronnie Kray shot a rival gangster at the bar of the Blind Beggar?
cards.fact: On 9 March 1966 Ronnie Kray walked into the Blind Beggar pub in Whitechapel and shot George Cornell, from the rival Richardson gang, as he sat at the bar, in front of witnesses.

about: Shopping in Knightsbridge and Kensington, a walk down to Chelsea.

cards.line: Did you know, a fatberg heavier than an elephant was pulled from under Cadogan Place?
cards.fact: In 2020 Thames Water found a 10-tonne fatberg of grease, fat and wet wipes under Cadogan Place in Belgravia. They said it weighed more than an African elephant.

cards.line: Did you know, Monty Python started in a flat on Basil Street?
cards.fact: In the 1960s, the first meetings that led to Monty Python's Flying Circus were held in a flat on Basil Street, Knightsbridge.

cards.line: Did you know, a robbery in Knightsbridge turned into a six-day siege?
cards.fact: In September 1975 a robbery at the Spaghetti House on Knightsbridge went wrong and the police arrived fast. It became a six-day siege, and every hostage was let go unharmed.

cards.line: Did you know, a fashion shop on Kensington High Street once drew a million customers a week?
cards.fact: In 1973 the fashion shop Biba moved into the seven-storey Derry & Toms building on Kensington High Street. Up to a million customers came every week, making it one of London's most visited sights.

cards.line: Did you know, Uncle Monty's house in Withnail and I is a real house in Chelsea?
cards.fact: In the 1987 film Withnail and I, West House in Chelsea is the London home of Withnail's Uncle Monty, played by Richard Griffiths.

about: A gig at Wembley the night before, then across town: Oxford Street, Blackheath, out to Thamesmead.

cards.line: Did you know, David Bowie first sang lead at a Blackheath pub, by accident?
cards.fact: In 1963 a 16-year-old David Bowie played sax with the Konrads at the Green Man. The singer cut himself on glass, so Bowie took over.

cards.line: Did you know, the Sun in the Sands junction is named after sheep?
cards.fact: The Sun in the Sands pub is named after sunsets seen through dust kicked up by sheep driven from Kent to London. The junction took the pub's name.

cards.line: Did you know, Thamesmead's concrete estate starred in A Clockwork Orange?
cards.fact: The Tavy Bridge area of Thamesmead, by Southmere Lake, was a setting for Stanley Kubrick's A Clockwork Orange in 1971. Its concrete blocks still turn up in films for their rough urban look.

cards.line: Did you know, the British half of Live Aid was played at Wembley in 1985?
cards.fact: On 13 July 1985 the old Wembley Stadium held the British part of Live Aid, with David Bowie, Queen, Paul McCartney, Elton John, the Who and U2.

cards.line: Did you know, the Sex Pistols, the Clash and the Damned all played one punk festival on Oxford Street?
cards.fact: On 20 and 21 September 1976 the 100 Club on Oxford Street held a two-night punk festival. The Sex Pistols headlined, with the Clash, Siouxsie and the Banshees, the Damned and Buzzcocks.
